newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN C.BANK SAYS COORDINATES WITH BANKS ON LEV.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN C.BANK SAYS COORDINATES WITH BANKS ON LEV.

text.p: Bulgaria's central bank met commercial banks on Friday and said they had agreed to coordinate action to prevent further sharp falls in the lev.
"The BNB board met the managers of commercial banks to discuss the situation on the foreign exchange market," said a statement from the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB).
"It was agreed that the BNB and commercial banks would take coordinated action to prevent further sharp falls in the lev," it said.
"The BNB board took measures to curb liquidity in the banking system and outside it," it said, giving no details.
A BNB spokesman said "outside the banking system" referred to financial institutions like exchange bureaus and financial houses but declined to elaborate on the measures agreed.

"The board continues discussing the current situation and if the foreign exchange market does not stabilise, the BNB will suggest measures other than its usual monetary instruments to rein in the crisis, which is the deepest since 1991 when the lev was floated against the dollar," the spokesman said.
Loss of confidence in the lev and rumours about the likely impact of a currency board, proposed by the International Monetary Fund to stabilise the economy, sparked panic this week.
The lev closed at 350-355 per dollar on the interbank market, in a narrower spread than 340-360 in early trade and up from 395 at the previous close. It opened at 272-275 on Monday.
